subject: Urgent: Novaplay latency spike — HOL blocking causing cascade
messages:

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency / 500s since 07:40 UTC — urgent

Summary of findings so far (quick):
- We observed a small set of long-sequence requests that are holding GPU worker threads for 1.2–1.8s each. Those long requests are arriving interleaved with normal short requests.
- Our default batching window is 15ms for this route; bursts of long sequences create head-of-line (HOL) blocking inside shared batch lanes. As the batcher waits, latency for short sequences balloons and backlog triggers internal timeouts which surface as 500s to the client.
- Concurrently, prefix-KV cache eviction rate spiked on two shards; eviction pressure looks like associativity conflict + low prefix TTL (30s) — short TTL + uneven request prefixes caused cache thrash, increasing decode time on miss.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:00 UTC:
1) Disabled shared batching for Novaplay route (switched to sequence-aware per-request lanes for small sequences).
2) Increased prefix cache TTL to 300s on affected shards and bumped associativity parameter to reduce cross-tenant conflicts.
3) Floated a temporary throughput cap on long-sequence requests (soft limit) to give the system time to recover.

Status: error rate reduced within 6 minutes; p99 improved but not back to baseline. Still seeing a few timed-out sessions while cache warms. Collecting eviction logs and GPU lane metrics, pushing to JIRA INFRA-5123.

Will follow up with a plan for permanent fixes.

—Rishi
Senior Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency / 500s since 07:40 UTC — urgent

Attached engine-config-diff.txt and short notes. Key root causes we should track for postmortem:
- HOL blocking in continuous batcher when high variance sequences share lanes; solution sketch: add short-sequence fast-path (reserved low-latency worker pool) and shape per-route batching thresholds.
- Cache policy: current LRU per-shard with small TTL makes prefix collisions catastrophic under spike; propose per-tenant prefix namespaces + adaptive TTL by prefix hotness.
- Scheduling: GPU worker fairness currently uses round-robin across queued batches; need priority preemption for latency-critical customer lanes.

Attachments: engine-config-diff.txt

Hannah
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lin <sara@novaplay.com>, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency / 500s since 07:40 UTC — urgent

Sara — sorry again for the disruption. Appreciate your on-call team for the quick reporting. Operationally: we reverted Novaplay to a conservative serving profile (per-sequence lanes + higher cache TTLs) and added a reserved low-latency pool so production recommendations aren't subject to HOL from exploratory long jobs.

We understand this was a high-impact outage for your promo window; we're preparing a formal incident report and an offer for a one-time credit per SLA terms while we stabilize the fixes. Markus and Rishi will follow with technical remediation and timeline.

Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Sales & Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@novaplay.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary + ask: Novaplay outage root cause and recommended exec approvals

TL;DR: Outage caused by HOL blocking + cache thrash on shared lanes. Short-term mitigations have restored customer throughput; we need two exec approvals to avoid reoccurrence and reduce SLA risk across other high-QPS tenants.

Asks:
1) Approve a one-week reservation of a two-GPU low-latency pool for Novaplay while we deploy adaptive batching (estimated cost impact: $7k/week) — approval needed from sales/finance execs.
2) Approve a rolling config change to increase default prefix cache TTL from 30s -> 120s and to deploy per-tenant prefix namespaces on the next infra rollout (requires brief config migration window).

Risk if we don't: repeated HOL cascades during peak spikes, larger SLA credits, and potential churn for high-value customers on bursty workloads.

Supporting artifacts: JIRA INFRA-5123 (tech notes), PagerDuty PD-7821 (incident timeline), attachments: sla-metrics-raw.csv, engine-config-diff.txt.

Markus
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
